task: P1.2 (issue #14) - prefill chunks as batch window rows (--prefill-rows)
verdict: NO-GO - decided at the economics gate before building, with measured numbers
machine: 4x MI50 32GB (gfx906), Threadripper Pro 3975WX, 125 GiB DDR4-3200, ROCm 7.2.0
recipe: --gpu 1 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-every 1000000 --no-prefill-borrow, STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 (BATCHING.md exactness recipe, same as every P0/P1 witness)
gate: docs/CONCURRENCY-PLAN.md P1.2 + task #14: --prefill-rows must show slot tok/s AND prompt tok/s >= the time-share control; the probe decision line was within ~1.5x build, far slower report NO-GO with numbers

probe.harness: tools/batch_interleave_test.py (A, B decode while C's 4888-token prompt is read; D/E test BYIELD)
probe.why_windowed_measures_the_ceiling: a --prefill-rows read advances at most 8 - (active decodes) prompt tokens per window and pays the same per-row service a verify window row pays (measured ~16 ms/row at b8, P0.2 b8 log line 128; the engine's own comment: a window ~16 ms/token vs a chunked run ~300 ms however few tokens, generate.cpp:11405-11409); the windowed arm (read_windows with --short-read 999999) reads the prompt through exactly those rows, so its rate upper-bounds the prompt side of any mixed window

arm_chunked.C_read: 4888 tokens in 26781 ms = 182.5 tok/s (5.48 ms/token) while slots A, B decoded
arm_chunked.interleave: the prompt was read in 8 parts, the slots decoding 8912 ms between them (second read: 6 parts, 6302 ms)

arm_windowed.side_finding: under --short-read 999999 a long read does not take BYIELD (D gave way: None) and does not interleave (2 slot tokens vs 398): read_windows has no yield/interleave points, only read_part does (BYIELD consumed at chunk boundaries, generate.cpp:11776-11824). The scenario then hit ERR BGEN: no such free slot and the arm exited 1. This is a property of the proxy flag, not of any default path (default --short-read is 64), and it is itself the reason --prefill-rows would need the MIXED window rather than more read_windows: BYIELD and the decode-share interleave live only in the chunked path.

comparison.prompt_side: 74.2-74.8 tok/s windowed vs 182.5-184.9 tok/s chunked on the same prompts at the same contention = 2.46-2.48x slower, past the 1.5x build line
comparison.slot_side: a mixed window at b8 costs ~131 ms (P0.2 log), so a decode row in it advances 1 token per 131 ms (~7.6 tok/s/lane); the time-share control already gave the two slots 398 tokens plus 8912 ms of whole windows between parts. The gate demands BOTH sides beat control; the prompt side loses 2.5x before the slot side is even reached
comparison.engine_comment_agreement: 13.5 ms/token measured for window rows vs the comment's ~16 ms/token; 5.5 ms/token chunked here vs ~300 ms fixed per run + streaming there

what_still_holds_from_the_source_map: the mixed layout is expressible TODAY (batch_rows.hpp validates a slot owning N contiguous rows - batch-mtp uses 2-row groups; keep-all commit = teacher-forced, verify.cpp:3167-3172; short parts already read through windows, --short-read 64). The finding is that on THIS machine's CPU-expert regime the row cost, not expressibility, kills the feature. On a VRAM-resident model (the paper's all-in-VRAM split, ~2.8 ms/row) the arithmetic differs - re-evaluate there before calling it dead engine-wide
not_tested: a real mixed window (prefill rows + decode rows together) - not built, by this gate's design; its prompt rate is upper-bounded by the windowed arm since it pays the same rows with fewer of them
closure: task #14 closes via its own NO-GO path (report NO-GO with the numbers, no engine change, default path untouched); docs/CONCURRENCY-PLAN.md P1 item 2 updated
